questions.prompt: Tests execute 45 of 60 executable statements. What is statement coverage?
questions.explanation: Coverage is 45 / 60 x 100 = 75%.

questions.prompt: A module has one if statement with no else. One test takes the true branch and executes every statement. What may still be missing?

options.text: Execution of every statement after the if

questions.explanation: Executing every statement does not require taking the false branch of an if without an else.

questions.prompt: For D = A AND B, tests use (T,T) and (F,T). Which target is met while B has not taken both values?

options.text: All-path coverage for every program containing D

questions.explanation: D is true once and false once, but B is always true. For runtime condition coverage, evaluation must also be observed.

questions.prompt: What does condition coverage require for a compound decision?

options.text: Only the whole decision is true once
Every loop runs its maximum count
Each atomic condition evaluates to true and false

questions.explanation: Condition coverage tracks the individual Boolean conditions.

questions.prompt: Assume both conditions are evaluated. For D = A OR B, tests use (T,F) and (F,T). What is missing?
questions.explanation: Both conditions take both values, but D stays true. Condition coverage need not imply decision coverage.

questions.prompt: What does condition/decision coverage combine?

options.text: Both outcomes of each decision and both values of each atomic condition
All paths and all input values
Only true conditions and true decisions

questions.explanation: It combines the requirements of condition coverage and decision coverage.

questions.prompt: With three independent Boolean conditions, how many input truth combinations exist?
questions.explanation: There are 2^3 = 8 combinations. Feasibility and runtime evaluation may affect executable coverage.

questions.prompt: For D = (A AND B) OR C, what is D when A=T, B=F, C=F?

options.text: It depends on the order of the tests

questions.explanation: T AND F is F; F OR F is F.

questions.prompt: For D = (marks >= 40 AND attendance >= 75) OR medicalLeave, which student is eligible?
questions.explanation: Medical leave alone makes the OR decision true under this stated rule.

questions.prompt: Assume all three conditions are evaluated, with every combination feasible. What is the minimum number of tests for condition coverage of (A AND B) OR C?
questions.explanation: TTT and FFF give every condition both values. The four tests in the notes are a valid example, not a universal minimum.

questions.prompt: In a short-circuit expression A AND B, A is false. What normally happens to B?
questions.explanation: Short-circuit AND skips its second operand when the first is false. An assigned input value is not proof of evaluation.

questions.prompt: In a short-circuit expression A OR B, which input forces B to be evaluated?
questions.explanation: B is needed only when A is false.

questions.prompt: Two independent if statements test x > 0 and x is even. Which set exercises all four feasible branch combinations?
questions.explanation: These represent positive/even, positive/odd, nonpositive/even and nonpositive/odd.

questions.prompt: A tester wants to exercise selected sequences of branches from entry to exit. Which technique fits?
questions.explanation: A path is a sequence through the control-flow graph.

questions.prompt: Why can exhaustive path coverage be impractical for a loop?

options.text: Path coverage ignores the loop body
Unbounded iterations can create infinitely many paths
Every loop has exactly two paths

questions.explanation: Different iteration counts generate different execution paths.

questions.prompt: A branch report shows 100% coverage. A required feature is absent from the code. What is the best conclusion?

options.text: Coverage alone cannot prove all requirements are implemented
The missing feature must have been tested

questions.explanation: Coverage measures the implementation that exists; requirements-based tests can reveal omissions.

questions.prompt: For ordinary executable control flow, what does 100% branch coverage imply?

options.text: Every atomic condition took both values

questions.explanation: Every statement lies on a traversed control-flow route, but stronger coverage targets and correctness are separate issues.

questions.prompt: A decision has four feasible outcomes. Tests execute three distinct outcomes. What is its outcome coverage?
questions.explanation: Three of four outcomes were exercised.

questions.prompt: For a simple if/else whose two arms each assign a different result, what is needed to execute both assignments?

options.text: At least one true-result test and one false-result test

questions.explanation: Each assignment is reachable through a different outcome of the decision.

questions.prompt: Which strategy best uses a code coverage report?

options.text: Add tests for meaningful uncovered logic and check requirements too
Stop all testing as soon as statements reach 100%
Ignore uncovered branches if current tests pass
Replace all functional tests with coverage numbers

questions.explanation: Coverage guides further testing but does not establish product correctness.

questions.prompt: What do nodes and directed edges in a control-flow graph represent?

options.text: Input partitions and their representative values
Program points or blocks, and transfers of control
Variable names and their assigned values
Test cases and their expected results

questions.explanation: A CFG models possible execution flow through the code.

questions.prompt: A flow graph has 7 nodes. What is the size of its graph matrix?
questions.explanation: A graph matrix has one row and one column per node.

questions.prompt: Using rows as source nodes and columns as destination nodes, what does M[2,5] indicate?

options.text: A direct edge from node 5 to node 2
A path necessarily passing through every node
A direct edge from node 2 to node 5

questions.explanation: The matrix convention must be stated; here the row is the source and the column is the destination.

questions.prompt: If a directed graph has an edge from A to B, what can be inferred about B to A?

options.text: Nothing without an explicit reverse edge

questions.explanation: Directed edges do not imply reverse connections.

questions.prompt: What does a nonzero diagonal entry in an adjacency matrix usually show?

options.text: An edge to the next node

questions.explanation: The row and column refer to the same node.

questions.prompt: A labeled graph has two parallel edges from node 2 to node 1. A simple binary matrix stores just one 1 there. What information is lost?

options.text: The fact that there are two distinct edges

questions.explanation: Binary adjacency shows existence, not multiplicity. Count distinct edges when computing complexity.

questions.prompt: A single connected, single-entry/single-exit CFG has E=10 and N=8. What is its cyclomatic complexity?
Two separate single-entry/single-exit CFGs have total E=9 and N=9. Using V = E - N + 2P, what is total V for P=2?
questions.explanation: V = 9 - 9 + 2(2) = 4. Do not treat two separate graphs as one connected graph.

questions.prompt: A connected structured routine has three binary decision nodes. What is its cyclomatic complexity?
questions.explanation: For this stated graph, V equals the number of binary decision nodes plus one.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes cyclomatic complexity?

options.text: The count of all possible input values
The number of defects in the program
The size of a basis set of independent control-flow paths
The number of seconds required for a test

questions.explanation: It measures structural complexity and guides basis-path testing; it does not count faults.

questions.prompt: A factorial routine initializes product=1 and repeats for index=1 through number. What should be returned for number=0?
questions.explanation: The body is skipped and product remains 1, matching 0! = 1.

questions.prompt: A graph contains an edge that no allowed input can execute. How should the test team handle it?

options.text: Invent a passing result for the edge
Assume every syntactic path is feasible
Claim the edge was executed by another test

questions.explanation: Some graph paths are infeasible because of constraints in the program or input domain.

questions.prompt: A team deliberately changes comparison operators and reruns tests to evaluate test strength. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Small code changes create mutants used to assess whether tests detect altered behavior.

questions.prompt: A test passes on the original program and fails on its mutant. What is the mutant's status?
questions.explanation: A failing test detects the changed behavior. The original should pass the test first.

questions.prompt: All covering tests pass on a mutant. What is the most suitable next action?

options.text: Investigate weak tests or possible equivalence
Automatically classify it as a real production defect

questions.explanation: A surviving mutant may expose a test gap, or it may be equivalent to the original.

questions.prompt: What is an equivalent mutant?

options.text: A mutant that one test killed
A changed program with the same observable behavior for every allowed input
A mutant with identical source text

questions.explanation: No valid behavioral test can distinguish a truly equivalent mutant.

questions.prompt: For this quiz, mutation score excludes known equivalent mutants. Which formula applies?
questions.explanation: This conventional adjusted score measures killed mutants among the non-equivalent mutants. Tools may report different denominators.

questions.prompt: There are 20 mutants, 4 are known equivalent, and 12 are killed. What is the adjusted mutation score?
All four non-equivalent mutants are killed. What is the score for that mutant set?
questions.explanation: 4 / 4 x 100 = 100%. This says nothing about faults outside the selected mutant set.

questions.prompt: A password rule is length >= 8. A mutant uses length > 8. Which input length distinguishes them?
questions.explanation: Exactly eight characters are accepted by the original and rejected by the mutant.

questions.prompt: Tests use only password lengths 5 and 10 for a >=8 rule mutated to >8. What happens?

options.text: The mutant can survive these tests
It must be equivalent for every input

questions.explanation: Both versions reject 5 and accept 10. The tests miss the boundary difference at 8.

questions.prompt: The original returns x+y and a mutant returns x-y. Which test with an expected value kills the mutant?
questions.explanation: The mutant returns 3 instead of 7. When y=0 the two expressions produce the same result.

questions.prompt: A test executes mutated code but checks no relevant output or state. What weakness may this reveal?
questions.explanation: A test must observe and check the behavioral difference, not merely reach the changed code.

questions.prompt: What does a 100% mutation score prove?

options.text: The selected non-equivalent mutants were detected under the stated scoring rule
Every real defect has been found
Every possible input has been tested
The program is safe to release under any conditions

questions.explanation: Mutation adequacy is limited by the selected operators, code, tests and scoring convention.

questions.prompt: A module sometimes uses an uninitialized variable. Which technique directly targets definitions and uses?
questions.explanation: Data-flow testing examines how variable values are defined, used and overwritten.

questions.prompt: In the statement total = price * quantity, which description is correct?

options.text: price and quantity are defined; total has a predicate use
All three variables have only predicate uses
No variable is used or defined
total is defined; price and quantity have computational uses

questions.explanation: The assignment defines total and reads price and quantity to compute its value.

questions.prompt: In if (balance >= amount), how are balance and amount used?
questions.explanation: They are read to decide which control-flow outcome to take.

questions.prompt: What makes a definition-to-use path definition-clear for variable x?

options.text: No redefinition of x occurs between that definition and the use
The path must contain a loop
The use must be a print statement

questions.explanation: A redefinition replaces the earlier value and breaks that definition-to-use association along the path.

questions.prompt: Consider x=1; x=2; print(x). Which definition supplies the printed value?
questions.explanation: The second assignment overwrites the first value before the use.

questions.prompt: Consider x=5; y=10; z=x+y; if (z>10). Which variable has the predicate use in the if?
questions.explanation: The condition reads z, not x or y directly.

questions.prompt: In x=5; y=10; z=x+y; if (z>10), can input data make the condition false without changing this code?

options.text: Yes; enter x=3 and y=5 even though assignments remain fixed
Yes; run the same test twice
Yes; ignore the assignment to y

questions.explanation: The constants force z=15. To vary these values, the routine would need parameters or another controllable input source.

questions.prompt: The data-flow table in the notes lists a predicate use of x at if(z>10). What is the correction?

options.text: The predicate use there is of y
The predicate use there is of z
There is no predicate in an if
x is defined by the comparison

questions.explanation: Use classification follows the variables actually read in the expression.

questions.prompt: Why identify def-use pairs before choosing tests?

options.text: To target paths linking assignments to later uses
To make all paths automatically feasible

questions.explanation: The pairs provide concrete structural targets for data-flow test design.

questions.prompt: A variable is assigned and then overwritten before any read. What should be investigated?

options.text: An unused definition or unnecessary assignment

questions.explanation: A definition with no intervening use may be redundant or may indicate a logic error; context determines whether it is a defect.

questions.prompt: A loop may fail to terminate because its counter is never updated. Which technique is most directly relevant?
questions.explanation: Loop testing targets initialization, iteration, boundary and termination behavior.

questions.prompt: A while loop can legally run zero times. Which case is especially useful for checking its entry condition?

options.text: The loop executes only its typical count
The condition is false before the first iteration
Only a very large positive count is used

questions.explanation: Zero iterations tests the skip path and initialization behavior outside the body.

questions.prompt: For a simple loop with maximum permitted count n=10, which set best targets small counts and the upper boundary?
questions.explanation: Use skip, one, two, near-limit, limit and just-over-limit cases. For 11, verify required rejection or handling rather than assuming it is valid.

questions.prompt: One loop runs inside the body of another. What structure is this?
questions.explanation: Nested loops execute an inner loop as part of an outer iteration.

questions.prompt: Two loops run one after another and share no control-dependent data. How can they first be tested?

options.text: Only with every Cartesian product of all iteration counts

questions.explanation: Independent concatenated loops can be tested individually; dependency requires additional combined tests.

questions.prompt: A second loop uses the final counter value from the first. What extra concern matters?

options.text: Only the color of the output
The second loop cannot have defects
The first loop never needs tests

questions.explanation: Boundary and state interactions across the loops must also be checked.

questions.prompt: For nested loops, what is a practical initial approach?

options.text: Test only the outermost loop at a huge count
Assume inner loops terminate because the outer loop does
Test the innermost loop while outer loops use small valid counts

questions.explanation: Work outward systematically and add tests for interactions and boundaries.

questions.prompt: In for(i=1; i<=rows; i++), rows=0. What does the shown loop actually do?

options.text: It executes its body zero times
It automatically reports an input error

questions.explanation: The condition 1<=0 is false. Rejection would require separate validation code.

questions.prompt: In nested loops i=1..rows and j=1..i, how many inner-body executions occur when rows=3?
questions.explanation: The counts are 1 + 2 + 3 = 6.

questions.prompt: Which statement about loop testing is accurate?

options.text: It can reveal off-by-one and termination defects
It guarantees that no infinite loop is possible for any input
It automatically limits production loop iterations
It is not useful for finding defects

questions.explanation: Testing can reveal defects; it does not change the code or prove correctness for all executions.

questions.prompt: Code is scanned for suspicious patterns before it runs. Which tool category fits?
questions.explanation: Static analyzers inspect code without executing the target program.

questions.prompt: A team needs to see which Java branches its tests executed. Which listed tool is designed for coverage measurement?

options.text: JUnit alone as a coverage meter

questions.explanation: JaCoCo reports Java code coverage. A test framework and a coverage tool serve different roles.

questions.prompt: A Java developer wants a framework for writing and running unit tests. Which listed tool fits?
questions.explanation: JUnit is a Java testing framework; it does not make every test white-box automatically.

questions.prompt: A Python team needs to organize and run automated tests. Which listed framework fits?
questions.explanation: pytest is a Python testing framework. Coverage measurement can be added separately.

questions.prompt: A team wants automated code mutations to assess test strength. Which pair of listed tools fits?

options.text: JUnit and NUnit as mutation engines
JaCoCo and EclEmma as mutation engines

questions.explanation: PIT and Stryker are mutation testing tools.

questions.prompt: A developer steps through code and inspects variable values during a failing test. Which kind of tool is being used?
questions.explanation: Debuggers such as GDB and LLDB help inspect execution and diagnose a failure.

questions.prompt: A design document is checked for missing validation before code exists. What kind of testing is this?
questions.explanation: Static testing examines work products without executing the target software.

questions.prompt: Which item can be examined by static testing?

options.text: Only a user interface after release

questions.explanation: Requirements, designs, source code, tests and manuals can all be reviewed.

questions.prompt: A requirement says the app must be fast but gives no measurable target. Which activity can find this issue early?

options.text: Only a driver calling a finished module

questions.explanation: A review can reveal ambiguity before implementation.

questions.prompt: A tool checks source code without running it. Is this included in static testing?

options.text: Yes, automated static analysis is included
No, static testing includes only three manual meeting types
No, source code must run before any checks
Only when customers attend the meeting

questions.explanation: Static testing includes manual reviews and tool-based static analysis.

questions.prompt: A team wants the most formal review, with defined roles, preparation, defect records and exit criteria. Which type fits?
questions.explanation: Inspections follow a rigorous, defined review process.

questions.prompt: Who normally manages and facilitates an inspection?
questions.explanation: The moderator guides the process and helps the group meet its objectives.

questions.prompt: Who records defects and action items during a formal review?
questions.explanation: The recorder maintains the defect and decision record.

questions.prompt: What is the author's usual role after accepted review defects are recorded?

options.text: Change the test results to pass
Approve their own work without follow-up

questions.explanation: Rework addresses the accepted findings; follow-up checks the corrections.

questions.prompt: What should reviewers normally do before a formal inspection meeting?

options.text: Wait until release to read it
Run stress tests instead of reading it
Study the work product individually using the review guidance
Rewrite the entire module without reporting defects

questions.explanation: Individual preparation improves the quality and efficiency of the meeting.

questions.prompt: A developer leads peers through code step by step to explain behavior and collect feedback. Which review fits?
questions.explanation: Walkthroughs are usually author-led and emphasize understanding, feedback and defect detection.

questions.prompt: A design needs evaluation by qualified peers for correctness, completeness and maintainability. Which review fits best?
questions.explanation: Technical reviews focus on technical quality. Management attendance does not define them.

questions.prompt: A team claims technical reviews mainly concern management oversight rather than technical correctness. What is the best correction?

options.text: Technical reviews focus on technical evaluation by qualified participants
Every review must exclude all technical experts
Walkthroughs are the only reviews that find defects

questions.explanation: The early slides conflict with the later, more accurate technical-review section.

questions.prompt: In an average function, reviewers find division by len(numbers). Which input is a key risk?

options.text: A list of four positive numbers only
A list with one valid number necessarily

questions.explanation: An empty list gives a zero divisor unless the function handles it first.

questions.prompt: The code adds braces and a semicolon but still accepts negative patient ages. What remains?

options.text: No remaining issue because syntax is fixed
A guaranteed runtime crash for all ages

questions.explanation: A syntax correction does not enforce the required age domain.

questions.prompt: A fund-transfer design checks balance but omits the daily limit. How should this be detected before coding?

options.text: Review the design against the business rules
Measure statement coverage of absent code
Assume the balance check covers the limit

questions.explanation: A checklist and traceability to requirements expose missing business checks.

questions.prompt: A transfer debits the source, then crediting the destination fails. Which design requirement addresses partial completion?

options.text: Atomic transaction with rollback on failure

questions.explanation: Debit and credit should succeed together or be rolled back according to the transaction design.

questions.prompt: Two transfers can read the same available balance at once. Which review concern is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Concurrent updates need controls that preserve balance consistency.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of review follow-up?

options.text: Remove all unresolved defects from the log
Check required corrections and review exit criteria

questions.explanation: Follow-up confirms actions are addressed and unresolved issues are tracked.

questions.prompt: A developer tests one bill-calculation function in isolation. Which testing level fits?
questions.explanation: Unit testing focuses on an individual component or function.

questions.prompt: Module B is ready, but its caller A is still under development. What test support is needed to call B with inputs?

options.text: Stub for B's caller that B calls

questions.explanation: A driver replaces the calling module and invokes the unit under test.

questions.prompt: Module B is ready, but lower module D called by B is unfinished. What should simulate D?
questions.explanation: A stub replaces a dependency called by the unit under test.

questions.prompt: A test harness reads values from a file and invokes a calculation routine. What role is it performing?
questions.explanation: Drivers can supply hard-coded, user-entered or file-based inputs.

questions.prompt: A payment module calls an unfinished tax service. A dummy service returns a chosen tax value. What is the dummy?
questions.explanation: The dummy replaces a called dependency and returns controlled behavior.

questions.prompt: Module B needs an unfinished caller and two unfinished callees. Which support may be needed?

options.text: No support because B is finished

questions.explanation: The driver invokes B; each stub simulates a dependency B calls.

questions.prompt: When should temporary stubs be replaced for integration confidence?

options.text: Only if the dummy prints text
As real dependencies become available, then test the real interactions

questions.explanation: A passing test with a stub does not prove the real dependency's interface or behavior.

questions.prompt: Why might a unit test use a stub that returns an error?

options.text: To exercise the unit's error-handling path
To guarantee that the real service never fails

questions.explanation: Controlled error responses allow repeatable tests of dependency-failure handling.

questions.prompt: A ready calsum(a,b,c) is tested while main is absent. Which temporary program is appropriate?

options.text: A stub that replaces calsum itself
A driver that calls calsum with test values and checks its return
A review of a different module

questions.explanation: The routine under test remains real; the driver provides the missing calling context.

questions.prompt: All unit tests pass with stubs. What still needs checking when the real modules are connected?

options.text: Interfaces, shared data and combined behavior
Only the spelling of module names
Only the length of the test file

questions.explanation: The real modules may disagree on types, formats, sequence or error handling.

questions.prompt: Two modules pass unit tests but exchange amounts in different units. Which testing level directly targets this issue?

options.text: Inspection of a user manual only
Standalone unit testing of an unrelated module

questions.explanation: Integration tests target interfaces and interactions between components.

questions.prompt: What is big-bang integration?

options.text: Adding one module at a time only
Starting only with the main module and stubs
Combining many modules at once and testing their interactions

questions.explanation: Combining everything at once can make fault isolation harder.

questions.prompt: Why can incremental integration help locate defects?

options.text: It eliminates the need for test cases
A smaller set of newly added interactions is examined at each step
It proves every module is bug-free

questions.explanation: The narrower change between integration steps helps isolate failures.

questions.prompt: The main controller is ready, but its lower modules are unfinished. Which approach naturally fits?

options.text: Big bang with every real module

questions.explanation: Top-down integration begins with higher-level modules and simulates missing callees.

questions.prompt: Low-level services are ready, but the high-level controller is unfinished. Which approach naturally fits?
questions.explanation: Drivers call the low-level services until the real callers are integrated.

questions.prompt: Testing begins from both the top and bottom, then connects at middle modules. Which approach is this?
questions.explanation: The hybrid approach combines top-down and bottom-up integration.

questions.prompt: Which mismatch is an integration concern?

options.text: A standalone function returns the wrong value even with correct inputs
Caller passes parameters in the wrong order for the callee
A requirements sentence is ambiguous before coding
A single loop fails to increment its local counter

questions.explanation: Interface mismatches can cause failures even when components work in isolation.

questions.prompt: An order module calls payment before validating the cart, contrary to the design. Which interaction aspect is wrong?
questions.explanation: Integration checks include the correct sequence of module interactions.

questions.prompt: A service fails, but its caller treats the error as success. What should an integration test check?

options.text: Error propagation and handling between the modules
Only the number of lines in the caller

questions.explanation: The caller must handle the callee's failure according to the interface contract.

questions.prompt: Purchase amount is 2000. Apply 10% discount, then 5% tax on the discounted amount. What is the final bill?
questions.explanation: Discounted amount is 1800; tax is 90; final bill is 1890.

questions.prompt: Under the same discount-then-tax rule, what is the final bill for amount 1000?
questions.explanation: The inclusive threshold gives a 100 discount; tax on 900 is 45.

questions.prompt: The discount module correctly returns 1800 for a 2000 purchase, but tax receives the original 2000. What should testing target?

options.text: Only the discount percentage in isolation
The data passed across the module interface

questions.explanation: The component output is correct, but the connection uses the wrong value.

questions.prompt: A tester checks a discount rule by comparing inputs and outputs with the SRS. Which testing type fits?
questions.explanation: Functional testing checks what the system is required to do.

questions.prompt: Can functional testing occur at unit, integration and system levels?

options.text: No, it is always only system testing
No, it is always only acceptance testing
Yes, the same test type can apply at several levels
No, it can only be static

questions.explanation: A test level describes scope; a test type describes the aspect being tested.

questions.prompt: A discount is 10% when amount >=1000; there is no tax in this question. Which whole-number set targets the threshold?
questions.explanation: The set checks just below, exactly at and just above the boundary.

questions.prompt: For that discount-only rule, what should final_bill(1001) return?
questions.explanation: 1001 - 10% of 1001 = 900.9. This question excludes tax.

questions.prompt: The function requires a nonnegative numeric amount. Which test checks an invalid input?
questions.explanation: A negative amount violates the stated input rule.

questions.prompt: The implementation raises TypeError for nonnumeric input. What should a test of final_bill('abc') expect?
questions.explanation: The type check runs before the business calculation.

questions.prompt: A calculated decimal result may have tiny floating-point differences. Which check is most suitable?

options.text: Require every floating-point representation to be identical
Always round all inputs to zero
Compare within the required tolerance or precision

questions.explanation: A tolerance-aware assertion matches the agreed numeric precision.

questions.prompt: A test's actual result differs from its expected result. What should the tester first establish?

options.text: Whether the software, expectation, data or environment caused the mismatch
That the developer must be wrong without investigation
That the test should always be marked pass
That every mismatch is an equivalent mutant

questions.explanation: A failed test needs analysis; the expected result or test setup can also be wrong.

questions.prompt: A defect report needs to help a developer reproduce a failure. Which details are most useful?

options.text: Only a message saying it does not work
Only the number of tests in the suite
Steps, inputs, expected result, actual result and relevant environment

questions.explanation: Reproducible facts make diagnosis and correction easier.

questions.prompt: A bug fix is delivered. Which pairing is correct?

options.text: Regression checks only the original bug; confirmation checks unrelated features
Both terms mean customer sign-off only
Confirmation testing checks the fix; regression testing checks side effects

questions.explanation: The two activities have different goals and can use overlapping tests.

questions.prompt: A complete integrated application is checked against its overall requirements. Which level fits?
questions.explanation: System testing considers the behavior of the complete system.

questions.prompt: A team checks login, search, checkout and order confirmation as a full workflow. What does this primarily test?
questions.explanation: The workflow crosses several components and checks a user-visible system function.

questions.prompt: The complete app is tested for both payment correctness and response time. Which description is accurate?

options.text: System testing is limited to performance
System testing is limited to acceptance sign-off
System testing can include functional and non-functional tests
System testing can never use internal knowledge

questions.explanation: System is a testing level; many test types and techniques can apply at that level.

questions.prompt: The requirement expects 500 simultaneous users. Tests measure behavior at that expected level. Which type fits best?
questions.explanation: Load testing evaluates behavior under specified or expected workloads.

questions.prompt: The expected load is 500 users, but the team deliberately increases it far beyond that to examine failure and recovery. Which type fits?
questions.explanation: Stress testing explores behavior beyond expected load or under constrained resources.

questions.prompt: A signed-in user tries to view another user's private account. Which type targets this risk?
questions.explanation: Authorization and data protection are security concerns.

questions.prompt: Users cannot find the checkout button or understand the error messages. Which type is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Usability examines how easily users can understand and complete tasks.

questions.prompt: A web app is checked in Chrome, Firefox and Edge. Which type fits?
questions.explanation: Compatibility tests examine behavior across browsers, devices or environments.

questions.prompt: After a server crash, the team checks restart behavior and data consistency. Which type fits?
questions.explanation: Recovery testing checks how the system returns to an acceptable state after failure.

questions.prompt: A team tests fresh installation, upgrade and uninstall behavior. Which type fits?
questions.explanation: The focus is the application's installation lifecycle.

questions.prompt: The app runs continuously for 24 hours while failures and resource use are monitored. What is the main concern?
questions.explanation: Long-running tests can reveal reliability, endurance and resource-leak problems.

questions.prompt: A system test plan lists scope, environment, schedule and entry/exit criteria. Why are exit criteria useful?

options.text: They identify prerequisites for starting testing
They specify how every individual test step is executed
They assign the root cause of each defect
They define agreed conditions for concluding the test activity

questions.explanation: Exit criteria support a transparent completion decision based on agreed evidence and risk.

questions.prompt: Bank employees perform realistic transfer tasks to decide whether the product supports their work. Which activity fits?
questions.explanation: UAT checks fitness for user and business needs using representative tasks.

questions.prompt: A product has passed system tests but users find its workflow unsuitable. What does this show?

options.text: Passing system tests does not guarantee user acceptance
Users must accept every product that compiles

questions.explanation: Acceptance focuses on business use and readiness, which earlier tests may not fully represent.

questions.prompt: Company staff evaluate a prerelease product in a controlled developer environment. Which acceptance form fits?
questions.explanation: Alpha testing occurs in the developer's environment with representative evaluators; it is not simply any internal test.

questions.prompt: Selected external users try a prerelease app in their own environments and give feedback. Which form fits?
questions.explanation: Beta testing uses external, realistic use to collect feedback and expose issues.

questions.prompt: A customer verifies a stated contract condition that the system supports a specified workload. Which acceptance form fits?
questions.explanation: The purpose is checking contractual obligations. Performance techniques may supply the evidence.

questions.prompt: A release is checked against applicable regulatory requirements. Which acceptance form fits?
questions.explanation: The objective is acceptance against applicable regulatory obligations; specific rules depend on the context.

questions.prompt: Which is the most useful acceptance criterion?

options.text: The application looks fine to one developer
There are exactly 1000 lines of code
All agreed critical workflows pass, with no unresolved critical defects under the release policy
The team has held three meetings

questions.explanation: Acceptance criteria should be clear, testable and agreed. Actual release thresholds depend on the project.

questions.prompt: Acceptance tests reveal a blocking business defect. What is the appropriate next step?

options.text: Release automatically because unit tests passed
Record the issue, resolve it and repeat relevant checks before the acceptance decision
Replace the customer with a stub

questions.explanation: The acceptance decision should use agreed criteria and the evidence after issue resolution.
